'''Operant conditioning''' describes the phenomenon that organisms learn to associate subconsciously behaviour with consequence and adjust their behaviour accordingly.

== Mechanisms ==

{| class="wikitable center"
|-
! 
! Positive (Presence)
! Negative (Removal)
! Consequence on frequency of behaviour
|-
! Reinforcement (Encouragment)
| Presence of pleasant stimulus
| Removal of unpleasant stimulus
| $\uparrow$
|-
! Punishment (Discouragement)
| Presence of unpleasant stimulus
| Removal of pleasant stimulus
| $\downarrow$
|}

== Experimental evidence ==

[[File:Skinner's operant conditioning box.png|thumbnail|300px|'''Skinner's operant conditioning box''': equipped with a food dispenser and mechanisms to produce various light and sound signals, all triggered by a lever/button (or some other action the conditiong process targets), [[Person:B. F. Skinner]]'s (somewhat uncomfortable) box can teach small animals (pigeons/mices, etc.) various simple to complex behaviour.]]

[[File:BF Skinner Foundation - Pigeon Ping Pong Clip.mp4|thumbnail|B.F Skinner's pigeons playing Ping-pong]]
In [[Source:The behavior of organisms: An experimental analysis (Book)|name-author]] and later replication studies, researchers were able to train various organisms to perform a variety of tasks via '''operant conditioning''', including teaching Pigeons to play Ping-pong.<ref>{{#cite:Q3496}}</ref>

== Application ==

=== Animal domestication ===

Pet training involves frequent '''operant conditioning'''.

e.g.,

* Giving a puppy a treat when it sits down after having heard "sit down" from the owner

=== Education ===

'''Operant conditioning''' is widely used in educational settings.

e.g., 

* Giving out prizes for academic excellence

=== Social organisation ===

Authorities (governments, employers...) in modern human societies employ a range of operant conditioning techniques.

e.g., 

* '''Positive reinforcement''': Monetary and honorary awards for contribution to the authority's set goals
* '''Negative reinforcement''': Tax reduction, fees exemption
* '''Positive punishment''':Prison (or even corporal punishment/execution in some places of the world)
* '''Negative punishment''': Reduction in pay/deprivation of benefits for not contributing as the authority expected
